# Film tour: restoring a perspective re-births a closed window

## Next step (2026-10-11 19:1xZ): place the re-born window from the Group's own hints

The open measurement has a cause in app code. `VesselWorkspace#getNativeWindowOpenConfig`, the opener behind Undo-after-close and a restore's `workspace-open` (`NativeVesselTransaction.embodyWorkspace`), returns a fixed `windowFeatures: 'width=700,height=600'` and no position. A user who closes a popup and presses Undo gets the window back at the browser's default spot, not where it was.

The Workstation already keeps where it was. `dockPlacement` (`Placement.forGroup`) holds `hints[workspaceKey] = {dx, dy, fallbackTarget}`, which are offsets against the main frame, refreshed on settled moves.

Prescription: `getNativeWindowOpenConfig` reads `dockPlacement.hints[reservation.workspaceKey]` and opens at `main.outerRect + {dx, dy}`. The main window's current `outerRect` comes from `Neo.manager.Window`. The engine clamps to the screen, as for tear-out vessels.

Size is not in the hints (`{dx, dy}` only). Carrying it would change the topology wire record (ADR 0029), so that stays a separate question. With a known position, the headless `stack-return` ending can then be measured as the film scene needs. This is still post-cut work.

## Status (2026-10-10 22:20Z): witness green; the beat waits for a re-born window's way home

The witness holds. `WorkstationPerspectivesNL` › "a topology restore returns the pane to its closed vessel, and opening that workspace re-births the window" goes through the film's own cues:
- the topology capture (it saves the working layout back, otherwise later auto-saves overwrite the capture);
- the restore, after which the pane sits in the closed vessel's workspace and no window opens;
- `workspace-open`, which re-births the window around the same live pane, with one owner throughout.

A user closing the re-born window brings its pane home within a second.

In the full film tour, the scene runs through the restore, the gate and the re-birth, and then has no clean ending:

| Ending | Outcome | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Title-bar `native-return` | refused | The re-born window has no native drag source. The resolver reads tear-out ownership records, and the first return cleared them. |
| `stack-return` (tab-strip drag) | the stack comes home, the emptied window stays open | `VesselWorkspace#retireReturnedVessel` closes only a window that has a tear-out vessel record. |
| Scripted close (`Neo.Main.windowNativeClose`) | refused | `getNativeWindowOpenConfig` passes no `nativeCapabilities`, so the route grants no close. Tear-out vessels open with `{close, position, resize}`. |

These are lifecycle gaps of a window re-opened for a restored vessel workspace, in code every topology window shares. They need their own leaf before this beat can ship, and that leaf is #19583, which blocks this ticket. Two related sightings:
- The tear-out's two concurrent vessel mounts leave a rejected `mountPromise` in the popup state. This predates neomjs/neo#19564.
- A `closeRequested` set after the window already detached is inherited by the next window of the same workspace.

**Reachable from the toolbar (22:47Z).** Undo after a user closes a popup re-opens it through the same `NativeVesselTransaction.embodyWorkspace` (`replayWorkspaceReturn`). Measured headless at `a852b8ca6e`: the re-opened window loads `?workspace=workstation-vessel:feed`, not the tear-out's `?popout=feed`. So a user reaches the kind of window those endings were measured on without any perspective. The endings themselves still need a headed run on this path; headless, they fail for a torn-out control as well. Two observations on the Undo path, causes not yet known:
- Both first-batch runs logged `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow: project() threw against a live owner`; neither tear-out control did.
- In 2 of 4 re-opens, the window showed its tab strip without the pane for 30 s.

The film proceeds without this scene; the additions are optional (the operator, 2026-10-10). The work is on the branch `ada/19569-film-perspective-rebirth`, not pushed.

## Context

On 2026-10-10 at 20:0xZ the operator set the film's length to 1:30–2:30, with the 83 s A6 narration kept whole (#15252). The plan of record grows the picture with witnessed addition leaves. This is the one named "the perspective across windows (restore re-births a window — witness first)".

The take candidate at `1c43d51e26` restores a perspective inside the main window only: capture → split → read → restore. A restore that brings a closed window back, with its pane, shows on screen the claim the narration makes about one runtime behind many windows.

## The Problem

It is unproven that a perspective restore brings a closed window back in the Workstation. The film must not stage a beat its engine cannot do, so this leaf begins with a witness.

## The Architectural Reality

- `DockService#restorePerspective` (`src/ai/client/DockService.mjs`) resolves a name across three sources: declared names, the window-scoped `layout.v1` collection, and the Group-scoped `topology.v1` collection.
  - A topology record reconciles against the workspaces that are live (`DockTopologyReconciler.reconcile`). A recorded workspace with no live match comes back as `unrestored`. The restore itself opens no window.
- `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` › "cold active selection retains the compact toolbar and programmatic window recovery…":
  - a semantic hydrate keeps a disconnected workspace's document but opens no popup;
  - `controller.openTopologyWorkspace(key)` then opens that workspace's window.
- `WorkstationPerspectivesNL` › "a shipped restore refuses to duplicate a pane its vessel owns…": a restore across a live popup never duplicates a pane.
- The film: `apps/workstation/tour/fiveBeatFilm.mjs` runs the `perspective-capture` / `perspective-restore` cues. `TourController#capturePerspectiveCue` and `#restorePerspectiveCue` drive them through `dockService.capturePerspective` and `restorePerspective` on the main workspace. Which collection that capture writes is part of what the witness pins.

## The Fix

1. **Witness first**, as a Workstation NL e2e spec:
   - tear a pane out into its own window;
   - capture a perspective that includes that window;
   - close the window, returning its pane;
   - restore the perspective.
   - Expect the window back with the same pane, and no pane with two owners.

   Compose the existing seams: topology capture, restore, then `openTopologyWorkspace` if the restore alone opens nothing. Pin which collection holds the record.
2. **If the witness holds**, add the beat to `fiveBeatFilm.mjs` after the in-main perspective scene, at the hand tempo of #19568. Extend `WorkstationFilmTourNL` to cover it.
3. **If it fails**, record here the mechanism that refuses, and split that mechanism into its own leaf. No beat ships before its witness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The witness spec passes at the PR head: the restored window carries the captured pane, and every pane keeps exactly one owner.
- [ ] The film tour carries the beat, and `WorkstationFilmTourNL` stays green with the beat's time in its log.
- [ ] Post-merge: the next headed take (#15252) shows the beat, and its clock is recorded there.

## Out of Scope

- The other four additions on #15252: a third window, the light-theme switch, the maximize beat, and the rail reveal held for its content.
- Pacing (#19568).
- Any change to restore semantics beyond what the witness shows is needed.
